II. Incurring losses does not by itself prevent Zakah from becoming due, so long as the institution's liabilities do not absorb all its assets.
III. The income statement forms the primary basis of Zakah calculation because social finance distribution depends on profitability.
IV. Because Zakah relates to ownership of zakatable assets, the financial statement that matters in Zakah calculation is the balance sheet rather than the income statement.
B: II and III only
C: I, II and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Question:
Regarding the eight heads of Zakah disbursement and the related rulings on social distribution, which of the following statements are correct?
I. Zakah is to be disbursed only to the eight heads specified by Shari'ah.
II. It is not necessary, in every case, to distribute Zakah to all eight heads simultaneously.
III. It is permissible to transfer Zakah from one head to another merely to maximize administrative convenience, even if that transfer defeats the intended entitlement of the proper head.
IV. The payer cannot discharge Zakah simply by waiving a debt owed to him by a poor debtor and counting that waiver itself as Zakah disbursement.
B: I, II and IV only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Question: A mining company extracts minerals: Batch 1 = value equal to 40g gold, Batch 2 = value equal to 50g gold. Total extraction value exceeds gold Nisab. Which is correct?
A: No Zakah because batches individually below Nisab
B: Zakah due because total exceeds 85g gold equivalent
C: Zakah due only after Hawl completion
D: Zakah at 5%
True answer: Zakah due because total exceeds 85g gold equivalent

Question: With respect to general exemptions from Zakah and related social-finance treatment, which one of the following statements is incorrect?
A: Zakah is not obligatory on public wealth or the insurance funds of public institutions.
B: Zakah is not obligatory on charitable Waqf, while in family Waqf the beneficiaries pay Zakah on the unexpended portion of Waqf income remaining at year-end.
C: The exemption applicable to charitable Waqf also extends to trust funds and public allocations for educational, charitable, and social institutions that have no specific owner, even if such institutions make profits.
D: Zakah is obligatory on revenue-generating fixed assets themselves, because the social objective of those assets makes them analogous to articles of trade.
True answer: Zakah is obligatory on revenue-generating fixed assets themselves, because the social objective of those assets makes them analogous to articles of trade.

Question:
An IFI holds at year-end: Cash = PKR equivalent of 50g gold, Trade inventory = PKR equivalent of 20g gold, Receivables (collectible) = PKR equivalent of 10g gold. The institution maintained ownership above Nisab at the beginning of the year and throughout. Which of the following statements are correct?
I. Zakah is due because zakatable monetary assets are aggregated to determine Nisab.
II. The applicable Nisab is 85 grams of gold or its equivalent.
III. Zakah is not due because none of the items individually reaches Nisab.
IV. Once Nisab and Hawl are satisfied, Zakah is calculated on the total combined value at 2.5%.
B: II and IV only
C: I, II and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Question:
An IFI has: Monetary assets above Nisab, Uses solar year, Agricultural produce (mixed irrigation), Minerals exceeding gold Nisab. Which are correct?
I. Monetary assets → 2.577%
II. Mixed irrigation → 7.5%
III. The Nisab for minerals is what has reached in value 85 kilograms of gold.
IV. The Zakah rate applicable to minerals is 2.5%
B: I, II and III only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II, III and IV

Question: A debtor mortgages the same identified warehouse to two creditors. Both mortgages are of the same rank. Later, he wants to sell the warehouse to a third party. One creditor consents, the other does not. The buyer is willing to take the asset subject to the mortgage if validly transferred. Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
A: Consent of only one creditor is sufficient because mortgages of equal rank are divisible by default.
B: Consent of all same-rank mortgagees is required, and if ownership transfers with their permission the mortgage continues only if the new owner accepts it.
C: No consent is needed because the mortgagor remains owner during mortgage and may freely transfer title.
D: Sale is prohibited in all cases because a mortgaged asset can never be transferred to a new owner.
True answer: Consent of all same-rank mortgagees is required, and if ownership transfers with their permission the mortgage continues only if the new owner accepts it.

Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe mortgage (rahn) under the Standard?
I. Mortgage means tying a financial asset to a debt so that the asset or its value is used for repayment in case of default.
II. The mortgage contract is binding for both mortgagor and mortgagee once concluded, and neither may revoke unilaterally.
III. Possession of the mortgaged asset may be actual or legal through registration and documentation.
IV. The mortgagee may appoint an agent to possess the mortgage on his behalf.
B: I, III and IV only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, III and IV only

Question:
A company obtains financing from an Islamic bank and mortgages a warehouse. Later, the company becomes bankrupt. The warehouse is sold for an amount exceeding the debt owed to the bank. At the same time, the company had earlier mortgaged the same warehouse to another creditor of equal rank. Both creditors demand payment. Which of the following statements correctly describe the Sharīah ruling?
I. The mortgagee has priority over other creditors in recovering his debt from the sale proceeds of the mortgaged asset.
II. If more than one creditor holds mortgages of the same rank over the same asset, their rights are shared proportionately according to their debts.
III. If the sale proceeds exceed the debt secured by the mortgage, the excess amount must be returned to the mortgagor.
IV. In bankruptcy, the mortgage loses priority and the mortgagee becomes equal to other unsecured creditors.
B: I, II and III only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the debt secured by mortgage?
I. The secured debt must be a permissible debt such as sale income, guarantee against damage, Salam commodity, Istisna'a commodity, or an owed usufruct.
II. A valid mortgage need not necessarily be preceded by establishment of the debt; it may be signed before or at the same time as the debt contract.
III. It is permissible to stipulate mortgage as a condition in trust-based contracts such as agency, deposit, Musharakah, Mudarabah, and leasing without restriction.
IV. It is permissible to stipulate mortgage in trust-based contracts if it is confined to indemnity in case of transgression, negligence, or breach of contract.
B: I and III only
C: II and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe special forms of mortgage?
I. The mortgagor may mortgage an asset owed to him by the mortgagee, whether kept as trust or as guaranteed asset.
II. The mortgagor may mortgage a borrowed asset or a rented asset, with the owner's permission in both cases.
III. In a sale contract, the seller may stipulate that after actual or constructive possession, the buyer should mortgage the sold good against the deferred price.
IV. Appreciation in the value of the mortgaged asset and its income are excluded from mortgage unless expressly included.
B: II and III only
C: I, II and III only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Question: Upon default, a mortgagee demands immediate transfer of title in the mortgaged land to himself at the previously agreed debt amount. The land's market value is higher than the debt. The mortgagor instead offers that the land be sold, with the creditor taking his debt and any excess returned. Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
A: The mortgagee may stipulate automatic ownership in default because mortgage is meant to document debt and avoid litigation.
B: The mortgagee may not stipulate ownership upon default, but may purchase the mortgaged asset at market value and take the portion to which he is entitled.
C: The mortgagee may appropriate the asset up to the amount of the debt, keeping any excess because the debt has priority over the whole collateral.
D: Bankruptcy of the mortgagor eliminates the mortgagee's priority and places him equally with unsecured creditors for the whole amount.
True answer: The mortgagee may not stipulate ownership upon default, but may purchase the mortgaged asset at market value and take the portion to which he is entitled.

Question: If the mortgage involves a property that yields monthly income, this income is:
A: The entitlement of the mortgagee (creditor) without any conditions.
B: The entitlement of the mortgagor (debtor), and the mortgagee (creditor) may not seize it.
C: Considered to be mortgaged along with the principal asset.
D: Considered to be a payment and discharge of the debt automatically.
True answer: Considered to be mortgaged along with the principal asset.

Question: Which of the following statements regarding the mortgaged asset and rights arising from it is incorrect?
A: A perishable commodity may be mortgaged because it can be sold and replaced by its value.
B: Appreciation in value and income generated from the mortgaged asset are included in the mortgage unless the parties agree otherwise.
C: If the mortgaged asset perishes without negligence of the mortgagee or his agent, the mortgage is extinguished but the debt remains valid.
D: If the mortgaged asset perishes while in the possession of the mortgagee without negligence, the debt itself is automatically extinguished because the collateral no longer exists.
True answer: If the mortgaged asset perishes while in the possession of the mortgagee without negligence, the debt itself is automatically extinguished because the collateral no longer exists.

Question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the general Sharīah rulings on mortgage?
A: The mortgagee may stipulate that the mortgagor appoint him or his representative as agent to sell the mortgaged asset in case of default without resorting to judiciary.
B: Death of either the mortgagor or the mortgagee does not invalidate the mortgage contract; the heirs substitute the deceased.
C: Once the debt is settled, the mortgagee may retain the mortgaged asset automatically as collateral for any future debt unless the mortgagor objects.
D: If the mortgaged asset perishes, the mortgage ceases unless compensation for it is obtained, such as through Islamic insurance.
True answer: Once the debt is settled, the mortgagee may retain the mortgaged asset automatically as collateral for any future debt unless the mortgagor objects.

Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe contemporary mortgage applications under the Standard?
I. It is permissible to mortgage Sharīah-compliant Sukuk and shares of Islamic financial institutions, and also shares of companies whose original activities are permissible.
II. It is impermissible to mortgage interest-based bonds, preference shares, enjoyment shares, and shares of companies predominantly engaged in ribā-based or other prohibited activities.
III. If a current account is mortgaged to the same institution where it is opened, the institution may use it freely because it already guarantees it.
IV. It is permissible to mortgage future income that is still to be owned if the principal income-earning asset is specified.
B: I and III only
C: II and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the mortgaged asset?
I. The mortgaged asset must be a Sharīah-permissible property, well specified and capable of delivery.
II. In principle, the mortgaged object should be tangible, yet it may also be a debt, a cash amount, a fungible asset, or a consumable commodity.
III. A share in common property may be mortgaged if it can be identified and sold separately.
IV. A perishable asset may not be mortgaged because its value cannot be preserved.
B: II and III only
C: I, II and III only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the trust status and liability relating to the mortgaged asset?
I. The mortgaged asset remains owned by the mortgagor as long as it is mortgaged.
II. The mortgaged asset is a trust in the hands of the mortgagee, notary, or agent.
III. If the asset perishes in the hands of the mortgagee without transgression or negligence, the debt is extinguished.
IV. If the asset perishes due to negligence of the mortgagee, notary, or agent, compensation is due at the value of the asset on the date of perish, while the debt remains valid.
B: I and III only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Question:
An Islamic bank extends a Murābahah facility to a client and takes a mortgage (rahn) over a commercial property. The bank holds the title deed as legal possession. The client continues to operate the property and receive rental income. Later, the bank requests to utilize the property free of charge until the debt is settled, while also stipulating that ownership of the property will automatically transfer to the bank in case of default. Which of the following statements correctly describe the Sharīah rulings under the Standard?
I. Legal possession through registration or holding title documentation is sufficient for establishing possession of the mortgaged asset.
II. The mortgagor may benefit from the mortgaged asset with the mortgagee's permission while the mortgage subsists.
III. The mortgagee may utilize the mortgaged asset free of charge with the mortgagor's consent because ownership remains with the mortgagor.
IV. The mortgagee is not permitted to stipulate that the mortgaged asset becomes his property automatically upon default.
B: I, II and IV only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Question: A bank accepts a mortgaged apartment from a client. The client later asks to continue living in it. Separately, the bank proposes that, instead of charging rent, it will itself use another mortgaged property free of charge because the client verbally consented. The bank also pays for urgent structural repairs and insurance documentation costs. Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
A: The mortgagor may benefit from the mortgaged asset only with the mortgagee's permission; the mortgagee may never benefit from it even for normal pay; and all expenses are borne by the mortgagee.
B: The mortgagor may benefit from the mortgaged asset with the mortgagee's permission; the mortgagee may not enjoy free benefit but may use it for normal pay with the mortgagor's permission; repair expenses are borne by the mortgagor while safekeeping/documentation/selling expenses are borne by the mortgagee unless otherwise agreed.
C: Both mortgagor and mortgagee may freely benefit from the mortgaged asset so long as the debt remains valid.
D: The mortgagee may use the mortgaged asset free of charge whenever the mortgagor consents, because consent cures the prohibition of lender benefit.
True answer: The mortgagor may benefit from the mortgaged asset with the mortgagee's permission; the mortgagee may not enjoy free benefit but may use it for normal pay with the mortgagor's permission; repair expenses are borne by the mortgagor while safekeeping/documentation/selling expenses are borne by the mortgagee unless otherwise agreed.

Question: A founder creates a charitable Waqf over a portfolio consisting of a current-account cash balance, Shari'ah-compliant company shares, and copyright revenues from authored educational content. He stipulates that part of the revenue may be added back to the Waqf principal and that the Waqf should continue even if one designated beneficiary body later ceases to exist. Which option states the best ruling?
A: The Waqf is invalid because current-account balances, company shares, and copyright-related revenues cannot validly constitute Waqf assets together.
B: The Waqf is valid because cash Waqf, Waqf of Shari'ah-compliant shares, and Waqf of moral rights are all permissible subjects.
C: The Waqf is invalid because adding part of the revenues back to the Waqf principal changes the donation into a revocable investment contract.
D: The Waqf is invalid because if one named beneficiary body ceases to exist, the entire Waqf necessarily lapses and returns to the Waqif.
True answer: The Waqf is valid because cash Waqf, Waqf of Shari'ah-compliant shares, and Waqf of moral rights are all permissible subjects.

Question: Party A", one of the officials of a Waqf school, submitted a request to the director of a charity fund affiliated with an IFI to donate educational equipment. The fund manager approved the request subject to the condition that Party A shall not incur any cost or proceed with purchase before the required funds are deposited. However, Party A proceeded to purchase equipment on credit before funds were deposited. The IFI later found it could not fulfill the donation. Party A then sought to compel the IFI through the judiciary. What is the correct ruling?
A: He has the right to request in court to compel the IFI to fulfill its promise to donate, because Party A incurred financial obligations on the account of the Waqf relying on the IFI's acceptance.
B: He does not have the right to request in court, because he proceeded to purchase on credit on the Waqf's account in an unauthorized manner, and also violated the IFI's explicit condition of not proceeding before funds were deposited.
C: He does not have the right to request in court, because a promise to donate is not judicially binding unless it is conditional upon an act performed based on the promise and results in a financial obligation, which is not satisfied in this case.
D: He does not have the right to request in court, because he failed to comply with the IFI's condition of waiting for deposit of funds, and therefore cannot rely on the promise to claim enforcement.
True answer: He does not have the right to request in court, because he proceeded to purchase on credit on the Waqf's account in an unauthorized manner, and also violated the IFI's explicit condition of not proceeding before funds were deposited.

Question: A Waqf was created as cash Waqf. The overseer invested the amount in real estate. After some years, the value of the property declined significantly, while another investment opportunity arose that could restore and enhance returns. The overseer proposed selling the property and reinvesting the proceeds. Some beneficiaries objected, claiming that the property had already become the Waqf asset and cannot be disposed of. As a Shari'ah advisor, what is the correct ruling?
A: The property cannot be sold because once purchased, it becomes the permanent Waqf asset and substitution is not allowed.
B: The property may be sold because in cash Waqf the original Waqf asset remains the cash, and substitution is permissible if it serves the Waqf's interest.
C: The property cannot be sold unless all beneficiaries unanimously agree, as their rights attach to the specific asset.
D: The property must be retained because decline in value does not justify substitution of Waqf assets under any circumstances.
True answer: The property may be sold because in cash Waqf the original Waqf asset remains the cash, and substitution is permissible if it serves the Waqf's interest.

Question: A wealthy individual declared that his commercial building shall become a Waqf starting next year, provided that regulatory approval is obtained. Before that date, he died, leaving debts exceeding one-third of his estate. The heirs insisted on executing the Waqf fully, while creditors objected. As a Shari'ah advisor, what is the correct ruling?
A: The Waqf must be executed in full because Waqf becomes binding once declared, regardless of death or outstanding debts.
B: The Waqf is treated as a bequest since it is contingent upon death, and therefore it can only be executed within one-third of the estate unless creditors approve otherwise.
C: The Waqf is invalid because Waqf cannot be deferred to a future date nor made subject to regulatory approval.
D: The Waqf must be executed in full because heirs have accepted it, and their acceptance overrides creditor objections.
True answer: The Waqf is treated as a bequest since it is contingent upon death, and therefore it can only be executed within one-third of the estate unless creditors approve otherwise.

Question:
Regarding the creation, legal effect, and classification of Waqf, which of the following statements are correct?
I. Waqf is the appropriation of an asset and donation of its benefit.
II. In principle, Waqf is recommended, and once validly created it becomes binding on the Waqif, who cannot resile from it.
III. Joint Waqf is one in which charitable and private beneficiaries jointly share the revenue and benefit of the Waqf.
IV. Waqf is not recognized as an autonomous juridical person, because its liabilities attach only to the overseer.
B: I and IV only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Question: A Waqf overseer leased a Waqf-owned commercial property to a company owned by his spouse at a rent slightly below market rate, claiming that the arrangement ensured long-term tenancy stability. The Waqif had stipulated that the overseer shall not be removed under any circumstances. A complaint was filed before the court alleging favouritism. As a Shari'ah advisor, what is the correct ruling?
A: The lease is valid because long-term stability benefits the Waqf, and the overseer cannot be removed due to the Waqif's stipulation.
B: The lease is invalid due to suspected favouritism, and the condition preventing removal of the overseer is void, allowing judicial removal.
C: The lease is valid because the rent is close to market value, and the overseer's fiduciary judgment cannot be challenged.
D: The lease is valid but must be adjusted to market rate, while the overseer remains protected from removal due to Waqif's condition.
True answer: The lease is invalid due to suspected favouritism, and the condition preventing removal of the overseer is void, allowing judicial removal.

Question:
With respect to the overseer (Nāẓir), his role, and his restrictions, which of the following statements are correct?
I. Waqf overseership is a right established for the interest of the Waqf.
II. The overseer holds Waqf assets in a fiduciary capacity and is not liable except in cases of misconduct, negligence, or breach of the Waqif's conditions.
III. The overseer may lease Waqf assets to himself or to closely related parties whenever the agreed rent is approximately fair, because the basic rule is permissibility.
IV. The Waqif may stipulate the overseer's remuneration, and if he does not, the relevant authority may specify it; otherwise it is determined at the prevailing market rate.
B: I and III only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Question: A Waqf has specific beneficiaries and limited revenues. The Waqf requires urgent maintenance, has administrative employees whose remuneration is among the avenues of disposal, and also has surplus revenues from prior years placed into a reserve. The overseer now wishes to use revenues and reserves while preserving the continuity of the Waqf and complying with the Waqif's stipulations. Which option states the best ruling?
A: The overseer must first distribute all current revenues to beneficiaries exactly as listed, and maintenance may only be funded if the Waqif expressly mentioned it.
B: The overseer must prioritize maintenance and preservation of the Waqf asset, then meet necessary obligations, while dealing with reserves and any shortfall under the Standard's rules.
C: The overseer must ignore existing reserves because reserve creation from Waqf revenues is invalid unless the Waqif expressly prohibited distribution to beneficiaries.
D: The overseer must distribute all revenues equally to beneficiaries and employees first, and only after that may he consider maintenance or future Waqf needs.
True answer: The overseer must prioritize maintenance and preservation of the Waqf asset, then meet necessary obligations, while dealing with reserves and any shortfall under the Standard's rules.

Question: Which one of the following statements is incorrect regarding the form of creation and conditions of Waqf?
A: Waqf may be created verbally, in writing, or by any means indicating the same, and it does not require acceptance by the Waqf beneficiary.
B: An unrestricted Waqf in which the Waqif does not specify the beneficiary is valid, and in that case it is directed to charitable causes as deemed fit by the overseer or the court.
C: If the Waqif makes the Waqf contingent upon his death, it is treated as a bequest, takes effect only on death, and may not exceed one-third of his estate.
D: Waqf must always be perpetual, and any temporary or condition-restricted Waqf is invalid even if the Waqif expressly stipulates such restriction.
True answer: Waqf must always be perpetual, and any temporary or condition-restricted Waqf is invalid even if the Waqif expressly stipulates such restriction.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question:
Which of the following conditions must be met for a third party's commitment for reparation of loss to be Sharīah-compliant?
I. The third party must be independent from the investment manager; if there is common shareholding, one party's ownership in the other must not exceed 50%.
II. The obligor must have no recourse to the investment manager for what he undertook.
III. The undertaking must be voluntary.
IV. Default or voidness of the third party undertaking invalidates the underlying investment contract.
B: II and III only
C: I, II and III only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question:
An investment manager in a Wakālah bi al-Istithmār (Investment Agency) arrangement inserts the following clauses and undertakings:
I. He undertakes in the contract to guarantee capital in all circumstances.
II. After a partial actual loss occurs, he voluntarily offers, on his own free will, to bear that loss.
III. He undertakes to purchase the underlying assets from investors at market value at the time of purchase.
IV. He undertakes to bear losses resulting from exchange rate fluctuations at the time of redemption.
Which of the following statements are correct?
B: I, II and III only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the rules on evidentiary burden?
I. As an initial presumption, the party claiming misconduct or negligence bears the evidentiary burden.
II. The evidentiary burden may shift to the investment manager if the contract stipulates it on absolute terms.
III. The evidentiary burden may shift to the investment manager where legislation, regulatory, or supervisory authorities make it mandatory.
IV. The evidentiary burden may shift to the investment manager where circumstantial evidence contradicts his claim, such as where he alleges loss while peer investments are profitable.
B: II and IV only
C: I, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II, III and IV

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe a service agent's undertaking under the Standard?
I. A service agent is confined to non-investment services such as leasing, insurance, maintenance, or collection of revenues.
II. A service agent may be treated as a third party that undertakes reparation of loss, subject to the prescribed conditions.
III. The service agent may simultaneously be the original party availing the financing in the same transaction and still qualify for the special ruling.
IV. If the service agency is for a fee, that fee must not exceed the prevailing market rate for similar services.
B: I and III only
C: II and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question: Which of the following is expressly mentioned as a contemporary form of misconduct or negligence by the investment manager?
A: Earning less than peer investments, even where all procedures were properly followed.
B: Not taking securities where necessary.
C: Failing to volunteer capital guarantee after a loss has occurred.
D: Refusing to provide expected profit projections to Rab al-Māl.
True answer: Not taking securities where necessary.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the rules relating to assumption of liability by the investment manager?
I. It is not permitted for the investment manager, explicitly or implicitly, to undertake assumption of risk after the investment contract.
II. It is prohibited for the investment manager to undertake to purchase the assets from Sukuk holders at a specified price fixed at the time of contract.
III. It is permissible for the investment manager to undertake to purchase the underlying assets at net asset value (NAV), market value, fair value, or a price agreed at the time of purchase.
IV. It is not permissible for the investment manager to undertake liability for losses arising from exchange rate fluctuations.
B: I, II and III only
C: I, II, III and IV
D: II, III and IV only
True answer: I, II, III and IV

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question: An investment manager enters into a Wakalah investment arrangement. The contract contains a clause requiring him to bear all losses absolutely. After execution of the contract, he issues a side letter undertaking to cover any exchange-rate loss on exit. Separately, after an actual partial loss later occurs, he offers voluntarily to compensate the investor from his own funds. Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
A: All three undertakings are valid because the manager's consent removes the Sharīah objection.
B: The contractual absolute guarantee and the side-letter undertaking are invalid, but the post-loss voluntary compensation is permissible.
C: The contractual guarantee is invalid, but the side-letter undertaking is valid because it is separate from the original contract.
D: The voluntary post-loss compensation is also impermissible because any assumption of liability by the manager is always forbidden.
True answer: The contractual absolute guarantee and the side-letter undertaking are invalid, but the post-loss voluntary compensation is permissible.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the further implications of liability and continuity of the contractual relationship?
I. Where funds were paid to be invested in the institution's general pool, and the institution failed to invest them there while the pool made a profit, the investor is entitled to a profit share according to the agreed ratio.
II. In the same situation, if there is a loss or damage, the investor bears it in proportion to his contributed capital amount.
III. Where the investment subject is a tangible asset, the relevant time for determining liability is the date on which loss, shortage, or destruction occurred due to misconduct.
IV. The investment manager is automatically dismissed once misconduct, negligence, or breach of conditions is established, even if the contract is silent.
B: I, II and III only
C: II and III only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question: An institution receives funds from an investor to be invested in the institution's general pool under an agreed profit-sharing ratio. The institution does not actually invest those funds in the general pool, but the pool later makes a profit. Separately, in another mandate, the same institution was instructed as agent to sell a tangible asset for not less than 500,000, yet it sold the asset for 470,000 without permission. The institution argues that only actual capital loss is compensable and that realized profit before the loss, as well as the shortfall from the instructed sale price, are not recoverable. Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
A: The investor is not entitled to any share of the general pool profit because his funds were not actually commingled, and the agent is not liable for selling below the instructed price unless fraud is proven.
B: The investor is entitled to profit according to the agreed ratio and bears loss proportionate to his capital, while the agent is liable for the difference between the instructed price and the actual sale price.
C: The investor is entitled only to capital preservation, not to profit, while the agent is liable for expected profit and opportunity cost in addition to the price difference.
D: The investor is entitled to full pool profit irrespective of his ratio, while the agent is automatically dismissed merely because he sold below the instructed price.
True answer: The investor is entitled to profit according to the agreed ratio and bears loss proportionate to his capital, while the agent is liable for the difference between the instructed price and the actual sale price.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question: Rab al-Māl instructed an investment agent to sell a tangible asset for not less than 1,000,000. The agent sold it for 960,000 without permission. Before the loss event, the asset had generated realized profit for the investors. Rab al-Māl also claims expected future profit and opportunity cost for what might have been earned had the sale been delayed. Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
A: The agent is liable only for the capital amount, because realized profit is never protected once the underlying is sold.
B: The agent is liable for the difference between the specified price and actual sale price, and liability includes realized profit before the loss but excludes opportunity cost and unrealized expected profit.
C: The agent is liable for the expected future profits because breach of instruction converts all hypothetical gains into guaranteed claims.
D: The agent is not liable because sale below specified price is merely a business judgment unless fraud is shown.
True answer: The agent is liable for the difference between the specified price and actual sale price, and liability includes realized profit before the loss but excludes opportunity cost and unrealized expected profit.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question: An investment manager structured an investment using Murābahah contracts together with an 'Urbūn (Earnest Money) sale arrangement to mitigate potential capital loss. If the market value of the purchased asset subsequently decreases and the buyer decides not to proceed with the final purchase, what would be the expected Sharīah outcome?
A: The investor bears a loss limited to the amount of the 'Urbūn only.
B: The investment manager must compensate the investor for the decline in asset value.
C: The investor suffers a complete loss of the invested capital.
D: The asset must be sold to the buyer at a previously agreed fixed price regardless of market conditions.
True answer: The investor bears a loss limited to the amount of the 'Urbūn only.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the third-party commitment for reparation of loss and the service agent?
A: It is permitted for a third party to commit to reparation of capital loss, shortfall in profits, or purchase of investment assets for a specified value, provided the third party is independent from the investment manager.
B: If there is common shareholding between the third party and the investment manager, the undertaking remains permissible only if the ownership holding of one party does not exceed 50% of the other.
C: A service agent may undertake reparation of loss even if he is originally the party availing the financing in the same transaction, as long as his undertaking is documented separately.
D: If the service agency is for a fee, the fee must not exceed the prevailing market rate for similar services.
True answer: A service agent may undertake reparation of loss even if he is originally the party availing the financing in the same transaction, as long as his undertaking is documented separately.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the basic rule of liability of the investment manager?
A: The possession of the investment manager is fiduciary possession.
B: The investment manager is not liable unless there is misconduct, negligence, or breach of conditions.
C: It is permitted to stipulate absolute liability on the investment manager so long as the parties expressly agree and the manager receives a fee.
D: After the occurrence of total or partial loss, the investment manager may voluntarily assume liability on his own free will.
True answer: It is permitted to stipulate absolute liability on the investment manager so long as the parties expressly agree and the manager receives a fee.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 61. Payment by Third Party
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the investment manager under the Standard?
I. The investment manager is anyone who undertakes investment of another person's funds with that person's permission.
II. The forms of investment management covered include Mudaraba, Investment Agency, and authorizing one of the partners to invest partnership funds.
III. Every service agent is necessarily an investment manager because he deals with investment assets.
IV. In Mudaraba, capital is provided by one side and labor is carried by the other side.
B: II and IV only
C: I, II and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 36. Impact of Contingent Incidents
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the consequences of partial entitlement of the object of commitment?
I. The commitment becomes null and void only in respect of the part owned by someone else.
II. The committing party has the option either to accept or decline the remaining part.
III. The committing party may accept the remaining part as part of his compensation.
IV. The committing party must necessarily terminate the contract because fragmentation of delivery leaves no room for option.
B: II and III only
C: I, II and III only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 36. Impact of Contingent Incidents
Question: An institution undertakes to supply all logistics requirements for an international conference on a fixed date. Before performance, a government authority unexpectedly prohibits all relevant imports, and the conference date passes without the supplies being deliverable. The failure was unavoidable, based on objective reasons, and caused by an external party. What is the most accurate ruling?
A: The commitment remains binding because contingent incidents only justify amendment, not termination.
B: The commitment becomes null and void because fulfillment became impossible or useless under the required conditions
C: The commitment remains binding, but only the price may be reduced proportionately.
D: The institution must still perform after the conference, since impossibility is judged only at the time of contracting.
True answer: The commitment becomes null and void because fulfillment became impossible or useless under the required conditions

Theme: Intensive course - SS 36. Impact of Contingent Incidents
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe Jawa'ih (calamities) under the Standard?
I. Jawa'ih refers to incidents other than human acts which cannot be avoided even if known.
II. In the sale of fruits and agricultural products, such incidents lead to discounting the price in proportion to the damage.
III. The concept is also applied by analogy in Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek where excess rent above normal rent is dropped if ownership cannot be transferred for a reason beyond the lessee's control.
IV. Jawa'ih applies only to agricultural produce and cannot be extended to other analogous contracts.
B: I and IV only
C: II and III only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 36. Impact of Contingent Incidents
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe contingencies leading to amendment of the contract?
I. Levy of customs duties or taxes after signing the contract affects the commitment of the party who must bear the new obligations by law or by contract.
II. Change in commodity prices causing serious harm to the contractor may be handled through reconciliation, arbitration, or legal arrangements.
III. Prevention of importation of goods to be delivered in Murabahah or Ijarah is treated as a contingency capable of leading to contractual amendment.
IV. Change in laws imposing additional financial burdens must always be borne equally by both parties.
B: II and III only
C: I, II and III only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 36. Impact of Contingent Incidents
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe contingent incidents under the Shari'ah Standard?
I. They are incidents that occur suddenly and significantly influence properly stipulated commitments.
II. They are identical to defects of will, except that their impact appears later.
III. They are different from termination of commitments by mutual consent.
IV. From the standpoint of their influence, they may either necessitate amendment of the contract or constitute an external reason for termination.
B: I and II only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, III and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 36. Impact of Contingent Incidents
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the rule on damage to the object of commitment?
I. If the object of commitment is damaged before delivery to the committing party, the loss is borne by the committed party.
II. If the object is completely damaged due to an act of the committing party, that party bears the loss.
III. If partial damage occurs before actual or legal delivery and is caused by an unavoidable heavenly factor, the committing party has a right of option.
IV. If partial damage occurs before delivery, the contract remains binding without any right of option because only total damage is recognized.
B: I and IV only
C: II and III only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 36. Impact of Contingent Incidents
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the overall structure of the Standard on contingent incidents?
I. Some contingent incidents merely require amendment of the contract rather than total termination.
II. Some contingent incidents constitute external reasons for termination without intervention by either party.
III. In the latter case, consequences are assigned to the competent party, as ownership-related consequences are borne by the owner.
IV. Contingent incidents include defects of will arising at contract formation so long as their effect appears later.
B: II, III and IV only
C: I, II and III only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 36. Impact of Contingent Incidents
Question: A lessee under an Ijarah contract faces an unexpected incident that causes abnormal harm in continuing the lease. The lessee's excuse is obvious. The lessor disputes the excuse and refuses termination Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
A: The lessee has no right of termination because contingent incidents never apply to Ijarah.
B: The lessee may terminate only if the lessor agrees, since excuses are always subject to mutual consent.
C: The harmed party has the right to terminate, and where acceptability of the excuse is doubtful the matter may be resolved by mutual agreement or resort to law.
D: The contract automatically continues because abnormal harm affects only price adjustment, not termination.
True answer: The harmed party has the right to terminate, and where acceptability of the excuse is doubtful the matter may be resolved by mutual agreement or resort to law.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 36. Impact of Contingent Incidents
Question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding contingencies leading to amendment of the contract?
A: Levy of customs duties or taxes after signing the contract may necessitate amendment.
B: Change in prices of commodities used in implementation, causing serious harm to the contractor, may be addressed through reconciliation, arbitration, or legal arrangements.
C: Prevention of importation of goods to be delivered under Murabahah or Ijarah may necessitate amendment rather than immediate automatic termination.
D: Any post-contract change in market conditions automatically nullifies the contract without regard to reconciliation, arbitration, or law.
True answer: Any post-contract change in market conditions automatically nullifies the contract without regard to reconciliation, arbitration, or law.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 36. Impact of Contingent Incidents
Question: If the object of commitment later turns out to be wholly owned by a third party rather than the committed party, what is the correct ruling?
A: The committing party must accept substitute performance without compensation.
B: The committing party becomes entitled to compensation.
C: The contract remains binding, but only if the third-party owner later ratifies it.
D: The committed party automatically acquires ownership by virtue of the original commitment.
True answer: The committing party becomes entitled to compensation.

Question: A trusting buyer (Mustarsil i.e., a purchaser who does not negotiate the price because he trusts the seller not to overcharge him.) buys an item at a price later found to exceed the highest expert valuation. After discovering the overcharge, he does not revoke for a period during which revocation was possible. He then grants a security interest in the item to a third party. Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
A: His option remains intact because attachment of third-party rights does not affect Khiyar al-Ghabn (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Price Gouging) until physical destruction occurs
B: His option lapses due to inaction after discovery, and attachment of a third-party right has the same legal effect as consumption
C: His option lapses only if the item is physically consumed; neither delay nor third-party rights affect it
D: He may keep the item and compel the seller to refund the excess market differential because Mustarsil cases are treated exceptionally
True answer: His option lapses due to inaction after discovery, and attachment of a third-party right has the same legal effect as consumption

Question: Which statement best reflects the standard's rule concerning transfer of trust-based options on death?
A: Khiyar al-Taghrir (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Verbal Deception) transfers to heirs, but Khiyar al-Tadlis (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Deceptive Conduct) and Khiyar al Ghabn (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Price Gouging) do not.
B: Only Khiyar al-Ghabn (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Price Gouging) transfers to heirs because it is based on measurable market loss.
C: All three trust-based options-Khiyar al-Taghrir (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Verbal Deception), Khiyar al-Tadlis (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Deceptive Conduct), and Khiyar al-Ghabn (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Price Gouging)-transfer to heirs if the holder had already discovered the ground of revocation.
D: None of Khiyar al-Taghrir (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Verbal Deception), Khiyar al-Tadlis (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Deceptive Conduct), or Khiyar al-Ghabn (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Price Gouging) transfers to heirs upon death of the holder.
True answer: None of Khiyar al-Taghrir (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Verbal Deception), Khiyar al-Tadlis (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Deceptive Conduct), or Khiyar al-Ghabn (Option to Revoke on Grounds of Price Gouging) transfers to heirs upon death of the holder.

Question:
Which of the following are valid prerequisites for Khiyar al-Tadlis (option to revoke on grounds of deceptive conduct)?
I. The deceptive conduct must result from the seller's conduct or instructions.
II. If the misleading condition arose from something beyond the seller's control or from unforeseen circumstances, the option is invalid.
III. The buyer must be unaware of the deception.
IV. The deception must still be continuing; if the item improves to a condition not less than the original specification before revocation, the buyer has no right of revocation.
B: I and IV only
C: II and III only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II, III and IV

Question: With respect to examples of verbal deception (Taghrir), which of the following is incorrect?
A: Increasing bids in an auction through phantom bidding (Najsh / Munajashah) B. Inaccurate statements falsely claiming that the item is no longer available elsewhere in the market
B: Inaccurate statements falsely claiming that the item is no longer available elsewhere in the market
C: False branding of products using counterfeit labels to promote sales
D: Deceptively inaccurate announcements about a company's performance to entice the public to buy its shares
True answer: False branding of products using counterfeit labels to promote sales

Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe Khiyar al-Taghrir (option to revoke on grounds of verbal deception)?
I. It is the right of a buyer to revoke a contract due to deception by the seller or a colluding party through inaccurate description of the sale item.
II. The deception must cause the buyer to purchase at a price higher than the market price.
III. It arises even where the seller's statements are accurate but the buyer later regrets the purchase.
IV. Deliberate misinformation regarding original cost in Murabahah, Tawliyah, or Hatitah is an example of Taghrir
B: I, II and IV only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe Khiyar al-Ghabn (option on grounds of price gouging)?
I. It arises where the price paid exceeds the highest estimate given by experts in the market.
II. The excessive overcharge must, according to certified valuators, be deemed excessive in commercial custom.
III. The buyer must be unaware of the price gouging at the inception of the contract.
IV. If the buyer accepts the contract after discovering the gouging, he may still unilaterally demand compensation for the excess.
B: I and IV only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Question:
Which of the following statements regarding the causes and lapse of Khiyar al-Taghrir are correct?
I. The buyer has the option to revoke the contract in the event of verbal deception.
II. The buyer may return the item within a period customarily acceptable for revocation.
III. The option lapses if the item is destroyed or consumed by the buyer before the deception is discovered.
IV. If the option lapses, the buyer remains entitled to partial refund equal to the deception margin.
B: II and III only
C: I, II and III only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Question: A buyer discovers that he was verbally deceived into purchasing an item. He promptly decides to revoke and return it to the place of sale. Which of the following best reflects the standard's ruling on return expenses and succession of the option?
A: The buyer bears the return expenses, and the option passes to his heirs if he dies before revocation
B: The seller bears the return expenses, but the option does not transfer to heirs upon death of its owner
C: The expenses are shared equally, and the option transfers only if the buyer had already notified the seller
D: The seller bears the expenses only if he personally uttered the deceptive statements, and the option always transfers to heirs
True answer: The seller bears the return expenses, but the option does not transfer to heirs upon death of its owner

Question: Which of the following is most accurately classified as an example of Khiyar al-Tadlis (Deceptive Conduct) rather than Taghrir (verbal deception) or Ghabn (Price Gouging)?
A: Collusion between brokers and sellers causing prices to rise above fair market levels
B: Falsely stating that a sale item is no longer available elsewhere in the market
C: Painting an old car to hide its age and give the impression that it is new
D: Deliberate misinformation regarding original cost price in a Murabahah sale
True answer: Painting an old car to hide its age and give the impression that it is new

Theme: Intensive course - SS 51. Option to Revoke (Defect)
Question: Which of the following best defines Option to Revoke Owing to Deal Fragmentation?
A: The option arising from breach of description in the subject matter of sale.
B: The option arising where a package deal no longer includes everything that was originally contracted for.
C: The option arising when the price is unfairly high compared to market value.
D: The option arising when a buyer fails to pay the price within the stipulated period.
True answer: The option arising where a package deal no longer includes everything that was originally contracted for.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 51. Option to Revoke (Defect)
Question: A buyer purchases multiple assets in a package transaction. After the contract, it is discovered that one of the items belongs to a third party. The buyer had no prior knowledge of this fact. What is the buyer entitled to do?
A: He must accept the remaining items without price adjustment.
B: He may revoke the entire contract or accept the remaining items and pay the corresponding portion of the price.
C: He may claim compensation but cannot revoke the contract.
D: The contract automatically becomes void.
True answer: He may revoke the entire contract or accept the remaining items and pay the corresponding portion of the price.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 51. Option to Revoke (Defect)
Question:
Which of the following situations may result in deal fragmentation giving the buyer the option to revoke?
I. When a seller sells his property together with another person's property without consent.
II. When it is discovered that part of the sold item belongs to a third party.
III. When part of the sold items is destroyed before delivery.
IV. When part of the Salam goods is unavailable on the delivery date.
B: II and III only
C: I, II, III and IV
D: I, III and IV only
True answer: I, II, III and IV

Theme: Intensive course - SS 51. Option to Revoke (Defect)
Question:
Which of the following situations cause Option to Revoke Due to Defect to cease (abate)?
I. The defect disappears before the item is returned.
II. The buyer explicitly waives the option.
III. The buyer implicitly accepts the item by continued use or exploitation.
IV. The defective item is destroyed by the buyer.
B: II and III only
C: I, II, III and IV
D: I, III and IV only
True answer: I, II, III and IV

Theme: Intensive course - SS 51. Option to Revoke (Defect)
Question:
Which of the following conditions must be fulfilled for Option to Revoke Due to Breach of Description?
I. The description must be permissible under Shari'ah.
II. The description must be specific and free from ambiguity (Gharar).
III. The description must relate to the buyer's purpose or affect price or quality.
IV. The breach of description must exist at or before delivery.
B: II and IV only
C: I, II, III and IV
D: I, II and III only
True answer: I, II, III and IV

Theme: Intensive course - SS 51. Option to Revoke (Defect)
Question:
Which of the following statements regarding Bay' al-Barā'ah (Sale on the Basis of "As-Is Where-Is") and defect liability are correct?
I. A contract may include a clause excluding the seller's liability for defect.
II. Such exclusion of liability is prohibited in Ijārah (Lease) contracts.
III. Such exclusion of liability is prohibited in Istisnā' (Manufacturing Contract).
IV. If a valid exclusion clause exists, the buyer still retains Option to Revoke Due to Defect automatically.
B: II and IV only
C: I, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 51. Option to Revoke (Defect)
Question: With respect to the conditions for returning defective items, which of the following statements is incorrect?
A: The item may not be returned if return would fragment a package deal without the seller's consent.
B: If the item is destroyed in the possession of the buyer, the buyer may only claim Arsh (Compensation for Inferiority Due to Defect).
C: If return due to defect is impossible, the buyer may claim compensation equal to the inferiority caused by the defect.
D: The buyer may return a defective item even if the defect was caused by the buyer.
True answer: The buyer may return a defective item even if the defect was caused by the buyer.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 51. Option to Revoke (Defect)
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe Option to Revoke Due to Defect?
I. It arises from a hidden defect that the buyer did not notice at the time of contract.
II. A defect is considered material if it diminishes the value of the item or renders it unfit for its intended purpose according to custom.
III. The buyer's right depends on whether the seller knew of the defect at the time of the contract.
IV. The defect must not have been caused by the buyer.
B: I and III only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 51. Option to Revoke (Defect)
Question:
Which of the following contracts may contain Option to Revoke Due to Defect?
I. Sale contracts
II. Money exchange (Ṣarf)
III. Division of wealth
IV. Hibat al-Thawāb (Gift Conditional upon Consideration)
B: I, II and III only
C: I, II, III and IV
D: II and III only
True answer: I, II, III and IV

Theme: Intensive course - SS 51. Option to Revoke (Defect)
Question: A buyer discovers after delivery that machinery purchased under a sale contract contains a hidden defect that significantly reduces its operational efficiency. The buyer had been unaware of the defect at the time of contract, and the defect was not caused by him. The machinery can only be repaired by incurring cost. Which of the following best describes the buyer's rights?
A: The buyer may only demand repair of the defect but cannot revoke the contract.
B: The buyer may revoke the contract or continue with it, depending on his choice.
C: The buyer must accept the machinery if the seller was unaware of the defect.
D: The buyer may revoke only if the contract explicitly grants such an option.
True answer: The buyer may revoke the contract or continue with it, depending on his choice.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 52. Option to Revoke (Misrepresentation)
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the rules relating to increase in the sold item during the Cooling-Off Option period?
I. Anything physically connected and growing out of the original belongs to the buyer if the buyer owns the option and confirms the contract.
II. Anything physically connected and growing out of the original belongs to the seller if the seller owns the option, whether he confirms or revokes.
III. Anything physically separate and not growing out of the original, such as compensation for third-party damage, belongs to the buyer in all cases regardless of whether he revokes or confirms.
IV. Anything separate but growing out of the original, such as dividends on shares and rent from leased assets, belongs to the seller.
B: I and III only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 52. Option to Revoke (Misrepresentation)
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the scope and immediate consequences of Cooling-Off Options?
I. Cooling-off options apply to binding financial contracts such as sale, lease, transfer of debt, guarantee, division of wealth, and Waqf.
II. They also apply to unpaid agency because unpaid agency benefits from reconsideration even though it is non-binding.
III. They do not apply to Salam or currency exchange.
IV. Where there is a cooling-off option, payment and delivery are not required unless the parties agree otherwise.
B: I, III and IV only
C: I, II and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, III and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 52. Option to Revoke (Misrepresentation)
Question:
Which of the following statements regarding Cooling-Off Options are correct?
I. A cooling-off option gives one or both parties, or a third party, the right to continue with or revoke the contract within a stipulated period.
II. It is affected by any phrase indicating that the contract is non-binding and revocable during the option period.
III. It is valid even if first introduced after the contract without subsequent agreement of the parties, because it is merely procedural.
IV. The option must be stipulated in the contract unless it is implied by pre-existing custom or the parties subsequently agree to include it.
B: I and III only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 52. Option to Revoke (Misrepresentation)
Question:
Which of the following statements regarding Option to Revoke Due to Non-Payment are correct?
I. It is an option stipulated by sellers or buyers to enable revocation if the other party fails to pay the price or rent on the due date.
II. It is valid only if expressly stipulated.
III. It is permissible in Salam and currency exchange, because non-payment is more serious in those contracts.
IV. It lapses upon the death of the owner of the option, whether seller or buyer.
B: II and IV only
C: I, II and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 52. Option to Revoke (Misrepresentation)
Question: An institution purchases a number of different non-fungible items from a supplier under a single deal and stipulates a Cooling-Off Option only over some of those items. During the option period, one of the covered items is destroyed before physical or constructive delivery. The institution had intended to offer the items to clients without first obtaining a binding promise from them to purchase. Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
A: The option is invalid because Cooling-Off Options cannot be used where the buyer intends resale to clients without a binding promise.
B: The option is valid only if the covered items are fungible and a percentage rather than specific items is stated.
C: The option is valid provided the items to which the option relates are specified; destruction of the sold item before physical or constructive delivery terminates the contract.
D: The option remains fully operative because pre-delivery destruction affects only delivery, not contract survival.
True answer: The option is valid provided the items to which the option relates are specified; destruction of the sold item before physical or constructive delivery terminates the contract.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 52. Option to Revoke (Misrepresentation)
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe Either-Or Options?
I. They entitle the buyer to conclude the contract to purchase one or more item out of several items specified by the contract during a stipulated period.
II. It is not required that the items be fungible or that their prices be equal, but where prices differ, the price of each item must be specified.
III. The option period must be specified, and there is no minimum or maximum time limit.
IV. They are created automatically by custom and do not require stipulation by the parties.
B: I and IV only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 52. Option to Revoke (Misrepresentation)
Question:
Which of the following statements concerning the effect of Cooling-Off Options on ownership and liability are correct?
I. If the option is owned by both parties or by the seller alone, ownership in neither countervalue transfers and legal rights related to the subject matter remain solely with the seller.
II. If the option is owned by the buyer alone, ownership of the sold item transfers to the buyer, and his conduct as owner serves as confirmation of the contract.
III. If the sold item is destroyed while in the possession of the seller, it is always the buyer's loss once the contract has been concluded.
IV. If the item is destroyed in the buyer's possession while the seller owns the option, and the destruction occurs without negligence or violation by the buyer, the buyer has no liability.
B: II and IV only
C: I, II and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 52. Option to Revoke (Misrepresentation)
Question: A seller and buyer conclude a sale contract and stipulate that the buyer may revoke the contract "when a market index reaches a specified level." No fixed date or definite period is stated. The contract also provides that the cooling-off period will begin three days after contract execution. Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
A: The option is valid because there is no minimum or maximum time limit for cooling-off options.
B: The option is invalid because the time limit is indeterminate, and the cooling-off period must coincide with the beginning of the contract period.
C: The option is valid if an expert can later determine when the index threshold is reached.
D: The option is valid because all timing defects can be cured by custom.
True answer: The option is invalid because the time limit is indeterminate, and the cooling-off period must coincide with the beginning of the contract period.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 52. Option to Revoke (Misrepresentation)
Question: With respect to the exercise and lapse of Cooling-Off Options, which of the following statements is incorrect?
A: The owner of the option may test the sold item without losing the right to revoke, unless he does so repetitively without need or behaves as an owner contrary to the contract and/or custom.
B: Offering the item for sale to third parties causes the option to lapse immediately, even before completion of any sale.
C: If the owner of the option does not revoke during the stipulated period, the option lapses and the contract becomes binding.
D: If one party voluntarily makes payment or delivery during the option period while the other withholds, the first party may demand return of what was paid or delivered.
True answer: Offering the item for sale to third parties causes the option to lapse immediately, even before completion of any sale.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 52. Option to Revoke (Misrepresentation)
Question: A buyer is granted an Either-Or Option over three specified items with different prices, with the right to select one item within a stipulated period. He takes delivery of all three items. Before making his choice, one item is destroyed in his possession without seller fault, and another is later treated by him as though he owns it. He then dies before completing the formal selection. Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
A: Because the buyer died before choosing, the option lapses and his heirs have no rights; he is liable only for the destroyed item's actual price.
B: The option transfers to his heirs; destruction of one item in his possession obliges him to purchase it for its price, and treating another item as owner is deemed confirmation for that item.
C: The option transfers to heirs only if all items were fungible and equally priced; otherwise the seller may revoke automatically.
D: Because he had delivery of all items, ownership of all three transferred to him outright and he must pay the price of all of them.
True answer: The option transfers to his heirs; destruction of one item in his possession obliges him to purchase it for its price, and treating another item as owner is deemed confirmation for that item.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 53. Option of Defect
Question: Which statement correctly describes the treatment of increase in the sold item during the option period?
A: Physically connected increase is considered part of the original asset.
B: Physically separate increase always belongs to the buyer.
C: Any increase must be divided equally between buyer and seller.
D: Increase is excluded from the contract unless specifically stipulated.
True answer: Physically connected increase is considered part of the original asset.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 53. Option of Defect
Question:
With respect to the permissibility of 'Arboun across different contracts, which statements are correct?
I. It is permissible in commutative contracts that do not require spot payment of countervalues.
II. It is permissible in contracts involving identified assets as well as assets sold by description for future delivery.
III. It is permissible in Salam contracts provided the remaining price is paid before delivery.
IV. It is impermissible in currency exchange contracts.
B: I and III only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 53. Option of Defect
Question: Which of the following rulings concerning 'Arboun arrangements and option trading are correct?
A: The buyer may freely trade the option arising from earnest money payment.
B: The buyer may stipulate refund of earnest money in certain conditions such as failure to obtain regulatory approvals.
C: The seller may substitute another asset with identical specifications without buyer consent.
D: Trading the option is permissible if the asset is identifiable.
True answer: The buyer may stipulate refund of earnest money in certain conditions such as failure to obtain regulatory approvals.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 53. Option of Defect
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the concept and legal treatment of 'Arboun (earnest money)?
I. 'Arboun is paid by the buyer to the seller at the time of contract on the basis that the buyer may revoke the contract within an agreed period.
II. If the buyer confirms the contract, the amount of 'Arboun becomes part of the sale price.
III. If the buyer fails to confirm the contract or does not pay the remaining price within the stipulated period, the seller may retain the 'Arboun.
IV. Money paid in connection with a mere promise to execute a contract in the future is considered valid 'Arboun.
B: I and IV only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 53. Option of Defect
Question: Which of the following best reflects the permissible form of payment for 'Arboun?
A: It must always be paid strictly in cash.
B: It must be paid only as part of the contract price in monetary form.
C: It may be paid in cash, in kind, or through usufruct.
D: It must be deposited with a third party until confirmation of the contract.
True answer: It may be paid in cash, in kind, or through usufruct.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 53. Option of Defect
Question:
If the option period expires without payment of the remaining price, which statements are correct?
I. The contract is considered revoked.
II. The buyer is not entitled to recover the earnest money.
III. The seller must return the earnest money if the buyer demonstrates financial hardship.
IV. If the seller agrees to extend the option period, the contract may continue.
B: I and II only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 53. Option of Defect
Question:
With regard to disposal of the sale item under 'Arboun arrangement, which statements are correct?
I. The seller may not dispose of an identified item during the option period.
II. If the seller disposes of it, the transaction is governed by rules of uncommissioned (Fodooli) disposal.
III. If the buyer ratifies such disposal, he loses his option and must pay the remaining price.
IV. If the buyer refuses to ratify the disposal, the second transaction becomes void.
B: II, III and IV only
C: I, II, III and IV
D: I and IV only
True answer: I, II, III and IV

Theme: Intensive course - SS 53. Option of Defect
Question:
Which of the following statements regarding the option period arising from 'Arboun payment are correct?
I. The option period must be determined by explicit agreement of the contracting parties.
II. If the parties do not expressly determine the period, established custom may determine it.
III. The option period may remain unspecified indefinitely without affecting the validity of the contract.
IV. Determining a specific option period helps avoid uncertainty and dispute.
B: I, II and IV only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 53. Option of Defect
Question:
Which statements correctly reflect the rules of liability and delivery during the option period?
I. Before delivery, the seller bears liability for the sold item.
II. If the item is destroyed before delivery, the contract becomes void and the earnest money must be returned.
III. After delivery, destruction of the item cancels the buyer's option and obligates payment of the remaining price.
IV. Mere delivery of the item automatically confirms the contract.
B: I and IV only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, II and III only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 53. Option of Defect
Question: A buyer paid earnest money for an identified property and later resold the property to a third party during the option period, without explicitly informing the seller that he had confirmed the contract. What is the correct ruling?
A: The resale has no legal implication on the option right.
B: The resale indicates confirmation of the contract and terminates the option.
C: The contract is automatically void due to resale.
D: The option remains until the buyer explicitly confirms it in writing.
True answer: The resale indicates confirmation of the contract and terminates the option.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 54. Revocation by Stipulated Option
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the applications of cooling-off options to revoke in leases and installment arrangements?
I. If the lessor stipulates that supplementary rent may be added at the beginning of each lease period to cover maintenance, insurance, and owner taxes, and the lessee refuses, the lessor is entitled to revoke the contract.
II. If the lessee had previously promised to purchase the leased asset, the lessor may exercise rights under that promise and demand performance, provided the supplementary rent for that lease period is not added to the purchase price.
III. A creditor may stipulate, after notifying the debtor, acceleration of all installments and the right to revoke the contract or one of them if the debtor fails to pay two or more installments despite being solvent.
IV. If the seller stipulates that the buyer must provide security, surety, or another guarantee and the buyer fails to provide it, the seller is entitled to revoke the contract.
B: II, III and IV only
C: I, II, III and IV
D: I, III and IV only
True answer: I, II, III and IV

Theme: Intensive course - SS 54. Revocation by Stipulated Option
Question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe revocation of contracts by exercise of a cooling-off option?
I. It refers to termination of a valid and binding contract by virtue of a stipulation in the contract giving one of the parties the option to revoke it.
II. It must be expressed only by use of the technical word "revocation"; otherwise it is ineffective.
III. It may be stipulated in any form that indicates it.
IV. Both parties may stipulate an option for one or both of them to revoke the contract in agreed situations, provided Shari'ah rules are not violated.
B: II, III and IV only
C: I, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, III and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 54. Revocation by Stipulated Option
Question: A lessee has a contractual right to revoke if the leased asset breaks down. The asset breaks down once, but the lessee chooses not to revoke and instead repairs it. Later, the asset breaks down again due to the same recurring problem. The lessor argues that the lessee permanently waived the revocation right after the first incident. What is the correct ruling?
A: The lessee permanently waived the option at the first incident because any non-exercise extinguishes the right absolutely.
B: The lessee did not waive the option because where the harm attributable to the cause is recurring or continuous, the option is not waived.
C: The option was converted into a compensation claim and can no longer be exercised as revocation.
D: The option survives only if the contract expressly restated the right after the first repair.
True answer: The lessee did not waive the option because where the harm attributable to the cause is recurring or continuous, the option is not waived.

Theme: Intensive course - SS 54. Revocation by Stipulated Option
Question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the overall legal architecture of revocation by exercise of a cooling-off option?
I. It is valid only where the stipulated cause exists, the conditions are fulfilled, and no impediment exists.
II. It remains valid even if contrary to Shari'ah, provided both parties had freely agreed to it in the contract.
III. If the period specified in the contract for exercise of the cooling-off option expires, revocation can no longer take place.
IV. Other situations of revocation applicable in options to reconsider, options to revoke for incomplete performance, and options to revoke for breach of trust are dealt with by their relevant Shari'ah Standards.
B: I, III and IV only
C: II, III and IV only
D: I, II, III and IV
True answer: I, III and IV only

Theme: Intensive course - SS 54. Revocation by Stipulated Option
Question: An institution includes in a credit facility agreement a clause giving it a right to revoke if the customer becomes potentially insolvent or breaches a restrictive covenant. The customer later breaches the covenant. The institution seeks to revoke but does not notify the customer. Which of the following is the most accurate ruling?
